text:
courtney: Quick sync from the postmortem — locking owners for remediation so we can close the loop. I grouped items into short-term (hotfix) and medium-term (policy). Please ack and flag blockers.

courtney: HOTFIXS:
- emergency quota backstop: open provider support + contact matrix (owner: ajay, ETA: 2026-03-24)
- fast scheduler tweak: decrease preempt window to 20-40s and enable soft-affinity (owner: liam, ETA: 2026-03-21)
- auto-degrade policy: graceful model-quality downgrade to smaller SKUs when headroom exhausted (owner: noor, ETA: 2026-03-28)

courtney: MEDIUM TERM:
- headroom policy: set per-cluster % + warm-cache warming plan (owner: noor, ETA: 2026-04-05)
- autoscale step-policy: add aggressive short-window steps (30s/2m/5m) and validate (owner: liam, ETA: 2026-03-30)
- recurring incident analysis: mine past 6 months for patterns and write recurrence playbook (owner: courtney, ETA: 2026-03-26)

ajay: Ack. I'll open the support ticket and add the escalation path. Will include a temporary backstop pool request too.

liam: Ack. Fast scheduler tweak: plan is preempt window 120s->30s (trial), soft-affinity on, and tweak binpack to favor larger contiguous allocations. Will post canary config to eng-infra and run against staging trace.

noor: Ack. Auto-degrade policy idea: when scale latency > threshold and headroom < 5%, switch certain low-critical routes to compressed/quantized model variant. This buys headroom without mass preemption. I'll draft policy and safety checks.

courtney: Love the degrade idea. Make sure we have a clear rollback and an observable flag to force revert.

liam: Canary plan posted: surge-microtune-v1. Metrics emitted: p50/p95 token latency, preemption_count, scale_latency, quality_delta. Rollback if p95 >6% or quality_delta >3% on sampled eval set.

ajay: Ticket created: https://cloud.vendor/support/CP-9000 (emergency quota). I added requested SKUs and provider contacts.

noor: For the auto-degrade, propose a two-tier approach: 1) reduce model size for non-core routes, 2) reduce response length on heavy routes. Both reversible. ETA for PR: 2026-03-27.

courtney: Can we also add a short test harness entry that replays the 03/18 spike and asserts the degrade decision path? If so, liam/noor coordinate.

liam: Yes. I'll wire the replay into the canary job. Example run: 

kubectl run surge-replay --image=redwood/loadgen:stable --restart=OnFailure -- /bin/sh -c "python replay_spike.py --trace trace-0318.json --replay-speed 1.5 --emit-metrics"

noor: I'll add a small eval job that samples 500 responses during canary and computes quality delta vs baseline.

ops-bot: Reminder set: "GPU backstop & microtune check" starting 2026-03-22 09:00 PT (recurrence: weekly). Assigned to: courtney, ajay, liam.

courtney: One more ask  for the recurring incident analysis, please include: common entry points, hot SKUs, region hotspots, and kube-preemption traces. If we see the same pattern twice in 6 months, that triggers an automatic postmortem.

ajay: Noted. I'll add a column in the incident tracker for "recurrence flag" and link the provider ticket.

liam: Blocker: staging needs 2 GPUs for a 3h window to run full canary sweep. Who can approve?

ajay: I'll escalate staging GPU booking with infra budget owners. Ping me preferred windows.

noor: Small note: auto-degrade must be tenant-aware; don't degrade enterprise customers unless explicitly allowed. I'll add allowlist logic.

courtney: Good call. Add allowlist and an override to force revert.

liam: Plan recap: 1) owners ack (done) 2) liam posts canary config + run by 03/21 3) ajay gets quota backstop in flight by 03/24 4) noor opens PR for auto-degrade by 03/27 5) courtney publishes recurrence analysis by 03/26 6) weekly sync until green.

ajay: I'll update the incident tracker and mark owners. If anything slips >48h, escalate to eng-sre lead.

courtney: Thanks all  will consolidate into the postmortem doc and send invites. :white_check_mark:
